correctness.rationale: The regular simplex analysis map is a scaled isometry onto the zero-sum hyperplane. Squared-error decrement is exactly the selected squared row residual. The key odd-cardinality inequality D>=S is reconstructed with a complete sorted-difference proof, explicit h_i,c_i bounds and monotonicity of T, including zero coordinates. A balanced-sign-and-zero vector attains the even-dimension beta>=2 bound; an equal-magnitude balanced-sign vector attains the odd-dimension beta>=1 bound. All beta are covered via subset monotonicity. Exact standalone finite checks pass; no finite check is substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The sharp sample-size saturation is a natural method-design question arising from the actual SKM trade-off between residual evaluations and guaranteed one-step improvement. The theorem holds in every dimension on the canonical minimally redundant tight frame, quantifies the exact parity effect, and proves a structural odd-cardinality square-dispersion inequality. It can benchmark sampled-greedy policies without claiming downstream runtime or multistep superiority.
